name: Standing Elevated Hamstring Stretch
summary: A standing unilateral stretch where one leg is rested on an elevated surface such as a barre or bench while hinging forward at the hips to stretch the posterior thigh.

setup: Stand tall facing a sturdy elevated surface such as a ballet barre, bench, or box set around hip or mid-thigh height.
Place the heel of one foot on top of the surface with the leg extended straight and toes pointed upward.
Keep the standing support leg straight with the foot pointing forward and hips squared to the front.
steps: Engage your core and maintain a tall, neutral spine.
Hinge forward at the hips, reaching your chest toward your elevated foot until you feel a gentle to moderate stretch along the back of the raised thigh.
Hold the position steadily without bouncing, breathing smoothly.
Carefully return your torso upright and lower the foot back to the floor before switching to the opposite leg.
instructions.breathing: Breathe deeply and rhythmically, exhaling slightly as you ease deeper into the hip hinge.
cues: Hinge at the hips, not the waist

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lower and upper back to reach further forward.
common_faults.correction: Initiate the movement purely from the hip hinge while maintaining a flat back, only moving as far as hamstring flexibility allows.

common_faults.fault: Opening or rotating the hips out to the side.
common_faults.correction: Keep both hip bones facing squarely toward the elevated foot throughout the hold.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending and locking out the supporting knee aggressively.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a soft, active knee on the standing leg to protect the joint and preserve balance.

precautions: Ensure the elevated surface is stable and will not slip or tip over.
Choose an elevation height appropriate for your current mobility to avoid strain.
